title: Canonicalize hierarchy resolution on the reduced dependency graph
description:
Make `resolve_hierarchy` compute the transitive reduction of its input edge set before resolving, so parent/children/cluster/rank become a pure function of the reachability relation, stable regardless of when edge reduction runs.

## Background

`resolve_hierarchy` (`crates/jit/src/graph/hierarchy.rs:423`) prefers direct edges when choosing a parent (`is_better_parent`, `hierarchy.rs:539-544`: distance 1 beats any transitive reach). Meanwhile `jit dep add` auto-reduction (`commands/dependency.rs:118-142`) and `jit validate --fix` delete redundant direct edges. The two subsystems disagree about whether a redundant-but-direct container edge is meaningful, so a node's resolved parent can flip when reduction prunes an edge (e.g. two same-level containers where one's directness is destroyed). Canonicalizing inside the resolver (reuse `compute_transitive_reduction`, `graph/mod.rs:345`) removes the instability without storage changes. The web UI consumes resolution from the server by the time this lands, so the algorithm changes in exactly one implementation.

## Success Criteria

- [ ] [hard] REQ-1: Resolution output is identical for an edge set and any transitively-redundant superset with the same reachability relation, verified by a property test over generated DAGs.
- [ ] [hard] REQ-2: The module contract in `graph/hierarchy.rs` states that resolution is defined on the transitively-reduced graph and explains the parent tie-break in those terms.
- [ ] [hard] REQ-3: The shared fixture `test-vectors/hierarchy_resolution.json` contains a case where a redundant direct container edge previously changed the resolved parent, and the vector test passes.
- [ ] [hard] REQ-4: Behavior on already-reduced graphs is unchanged: existing hierarchy unit and vector tests pass without semantic edits.

## Notes

Resolution stays pure (no I/O) and keeps its existing signature; the reduction is internal. Watch performance on large graphs: reduction is O(V*E) worst case, acceptable at jit repo scale, but avoid recomputing it per node.
